Package de.schladebeck.fx.grid.render

package de.schladebeck.fx.grid.render

Painting cells and column headers. A CellRenderer draws one cell onto the grid's canvas, given a CellContext with the cell's bounds, value, font and colors. CellRenderers has the built-in renderers and the text helpers that shorten or wrap text and feed tooltips and column fitting.

Which renderer and which style a cell gets is decided per cell: a CellRendererProvider or the column's renderer, and a CellStyleProvider returning shared CellStyle constants. Styles set colors, a font, or only its weight and posture, which keeps the grid's font size so bold text follows the theme.

CellStyle negative = CellStyle.DEFAULT.withTextFill(Color.web("#cf222e")).withFontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD);
grid.setCellStyleProvider((row, column, value) -> value instanceof Double d && d < 0 ? negative : null);
grid.getColumn(3).setRenderer(CellRenderers.number("#,##0.00"))
        .setHeaderStyle(CellStyle.DEFAULT.withAlignment(HPos.RIGHT));

Renderers run for every visible cell in every frame. They must not allocate much, must not keep the context, and should leave cutting text to CellContext.fitText(String) or, for text in another font, CellContext.fitText(String, javafx.scene.text.Font), so tooltips and fitting keep working. TextMetrics measures text with the same rules, for example to compute row heights. CellContext.indent(double) makes room for something painted before the content, such as an icon, so the text is fitted into the rest.

Implementation notes

CellContext is abstract so the painter can fill in one instance for every cell without setters in the API. Fonts with a style's weight or posture are derived once per style instance and base font and then cached; that is why styles should be constants and not built per cell.
